records.region: Venezuelan Andes and southern Lake Maracaibo region.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative system identity for the complete selected Mifafí headwater–Chama valley–Maracaibo outlet chain; not a uniform local hydronym for every reach or lateral tributary.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The original 2017 Chama chapter supplies overlapping cartography from the actual northeastern opening through the southward headwater connector and southwest-trending Andean valley, the separate Mocotíes junction, the northward gorge past El Vigía and the lowland outlet into southern Lago de Maracaibo. Figure 7 resolves the selected opening and its relationship to El Águila and Apartaderos; Figure 2 covers the complete receiving corridor and terminal. Bounded prose distinguishes the locally named quebrada Mifafí opening from the downstream Chama. Río Chama is supported as a representative system candidate, with no material geographic coverage gap.
records.completion_scope: The original 2017 Chama chapter supplies overlapping cartography from the actual northeastern opening through the southward headwater connector and southwest-trending Andean valley, the separate Mocotíes junction, the northward gorge past El Vigía and the lowland outlet into southern Lago de Maracaibo. Figure 7 resolves the selected opening and its relationship to El Águila and Apartaderos; Figure 2 covers the complete receiving corridor and terminal. Bounded prose distinguishes the locally named quebrada Mifafí opening from the downstream Chama. Río Chama is supported as a representative system candidate, with no material geographic coverage gap.

component_scope_limits: The chapter describes the initial northeast-then-south headwater course as cartographically known as quebrada Mifafí, with Chama used after the El Águila junction. Figure 7 uses R. Chama more broadly over this headwater chain. This supports a representative system designation rather than a precise or uniform whole-feature scalar name.

El Águila, La Toma and other upper feeders are separate tributaries. Mucujún, Albarregas, La González, Nuestra Señora, San Pablo and Mocotíes are distinct mapped branches, not aliases for the selected line.

The selected terminal is the Chama outlet into the southern part of Lago de Maracaibo. The lake is the receiving waterbody and is not renamed Chama; no open-Caribbean terminal is inferred from the retained sea-class metadata.

No intermediate lake or reservoir passage is depicted on the selected fluvial corridor in the acquired publication maps. This is a bounded cartographic observation, not an inventory of every water-management structure or a current-flow assertion.
The maps are generalized corridor evidence. Exact headmost springs, bank positions, hydronym-change vertices, delta distributary centerlines and modern shoreline/mouth vertices are not assigned.
No accepted name, Korean name, formal registry determination or official total length is established. The source’s river-length estimate is not substituted for retained model length.

records.candidate_name_role: Supported name of the downstream river and a provisional representative-system candidate; full selected-opening correspondence remains unresolved.
records.material_pending_reason: The full northeastern selected opening and its headward branch transfer onto the documented Cañazas corridor remain unestablished. The lower Cañazas, Bayano reservoir, downstream Bayano/Chepo and estuarine ending are mapped, but do not close that initial component gap.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected object runs through the Cañazas-side eastern drainage, Bayano reservoir and the downstream Río Bayano/Chepo estuarine corridor. Readable original cartography supports these broad components and distinguishes the separately entering upper Bayano and other tributaries. The northeastern selected opening and its headward branch transfer onto the documented Cañazas corridor are not unambiguously accounted for. This genuine component gap prevents completed representative identity or a completed naming-scope hold.

component_scope_limits: Río Bayano is not adopted as a uniform name for the eastern Cañazas-side branch, lake passage, other tributaries or every selected reach.
The basin map explicitly uses Río Bayano o Chepo for the lower river; this is reach-level cartographic usage, not an independently checked registry determination for the complete selected object.
Lago Bayano is an impoundment name. ARAP's description of IGN recognition concerns that reservoir, not formal registration of the whole modeled river system.
No unique name is assigned to the unresolved northeastern opening.
The selected ending is interpreted as an estuarine river setting. The retained model sea classification is not substituted for an observed exact open-coast mouth.

material_pending_components.gap: The full northeastern selected opening and its transfer to the documented Cañazas trunk remain without unambiguous primary cartographic correspondence.
material_pending_components.why_material: A basin label, nearby named branch, station point, or retained model connectivity does not establish this headward component. All other documented components do not remove that gap.
material_pending_components.needed_evidence: Readable original cartography that includes the selected northeastern headward corridor and its connection to the Cañazas-side network at ordinary corridor scale.

records.supported_name_scope: Representative downstream Jacu receiving system. The selected whole comprises an initially unnamed feeder, bounded Bonsucesso/Jacu/Campo Comprido/Japi reach settings, separate reservoir passages and a receiving lagoon.
records.region: Paraíba and Rio Grande do Norte, northeastern Brazil.
records.candidate_name_role: representative receiving river-system candidate, not a whole-route scalar hydronym
records.geographic_disambiguation: Original detailed and regional cartography positively covers the entire selected component, including the short initial feeder, named and unnamed local reaches, Bonsucesso waterbody, later Retiro reservoir passage, JapiII passage, material tributary junctions and southwest Guaraíras terminal. Rio Jacu is supported only as the representative receiving-system identity. The2019 original engineering plate and applicable primary prose supply the later Retiro placement that the2009 river maps alone cannot establish. All accepted/scalar/Korean names remain null and no product application is authorized.
records.completion_scope: Original detailed and regional cartography positively covers the entire selected component, including the short initial feeder, named and unnamed local reaches, Bonsucesso waterbody, later Retiro reservoir passage, JapiII passage, material tributary junctions and southwest Guaraíras terminal. Rio Jacu is supported only as the representative receiving-system identity. The2019 original engineering plate and applicable primary prose supply the later Retiro placement that the2009 river maps alone cannot establish. component_scope_limits: Do not assign Rio Jacu uniformly to the initial feeder, every local tributary, Retiro, JapiII or Guaraíras.
Rio Bonsucesso and Rio do Trapiá are actual local stream labels; Bola/Bolas are settlement labels, not a newly invented river name.

Retiro and JapiII are distinct impoundments. Boqueirão do Cais is on the separately joining Campo Comprido approach; its adutora from Retiro is an artificial transfer, not the selected downstream natural route.
No formal naming-register status, accepted alias list, exact source spring, exact name-change boundary or official river length established.
The model’s sea terminal metadata does not override the actual mapped receiving-lagoon setting.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
